Comparator detects concurrency because neither vector dominates.

lesson.scenario: A Dynamo-style document store uses client causal context to distinguish overwrites from concurrent writes.
entities: Vector returned with reads and writes

steps.title: Return causal context with a read
steps.narration: The coordinator returns body revision 11 together with opaque context {8,3}; the client must echo it to update what it observed.

coord.detail: No work accepted in this phase

steps.outcome: The next write can identify its causal predecessor.
steps.invariant: Writes increment one replica component above the component-wise maximum of supplied context; only dominated versions are discarded, and incomparable vectors remain visible siblings until a descendant covers every branch.

steps.title: Create a causal overwrite
steps.narration: R1 takes the component-wise maximum, increments R1, and stores {9,3}; this vector dominates {8,3}.
action: PUT D9 with context {8,3} via R1
steps.outcome: The old version can be removed safely.
steps.invariant: Writes increment one replica component above the component-wise maximum of supplied context; only dominated versions are discarded, and incomparable vectors remain visible siblings until a descendant covers every branch.

steps.title: Accept a disconnected concurrent write
steps.narration: A disconnected client updates a different field; R2 increments its component to create {8,4}, which is incomparable with {9,3}.
action: PUT D9 through R2 with stale context {8,3}
steps.outcome: Availability produces an explicit sibling instead of silent loss.
steps.invariant: Writes increment one replica component above the component-wise maximum of supplied context; only dominated versions are discarded, and incomparable vectors remain visible siblings until a descendant covers every branch.

steps.title: Return only maximal siblings
steps.narration: Neither sibling dominates the other, so the read returns both bodies and merged context max({9,3},{8,4})={9,4}.
steps.outcome: The conflict is visible to the domain resolver.
steps.invariant: Writes increment one replica component above the component-wise maximum of supplied context; only dominated versions are discarded, and incomparable vectors remain visible siblings until a descendant covers every branch.

steps.title: Resolve with a causal descendant
steps.narration: R1 increments to {10,4}; this new vector dominates both {9,3} and {8,4}, allowing replicas to compact them after replication.
steps.outcome: The document returns to one converged version.
steps.invariant: Writes increment one replica component above the component-wise maximum of supplied context; only dominated versions are discarded, and incomparable vectors remain visible siblings until a descendant covers every branch.

production.scenario: Dropbox Paper annotation sync needs to explain whether two edits are ordered or truly concurrent before showing reviewers a merge choice.
components: global authors editing comments and highlights from browsers, tablets, and desktop clients
service boundary that accepts document deltas and enforces membership and size policies
control-plane service that uses vector clocks to distinguish ordered updates from concurrent branches
durable authority in Spanner for annotation events, versions, and merge outcomes
shows the winning annotation state or presents concurrent branches to human reviewers
support-side worker that replays high-value annotation branches when automatic resolution is not acceptable
observability path for concurrent branch rate and unresolved merge backlog
flows: Editors save annotation changes that may have been produced offline or on multiple devices.
The sync edge asks the vector clock service whether the update is in-order or concurrent.
The lineage decision and accepted event are persisted in the authoritative annotation history.
Review UIs load the current annotation projection or a concurrent merge choice from durable history.
Documents with unacceptable automatic outcomes are escalated to a support worker for replay.
Support and policy tools rerun competing branches through the same lineage service with new inputs.
Diagnostics report concurrency hotspots, reviewer load, and time to merge acceptance.
